sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's growing data center buildout is driving structural demand for storage and semiconductor components, benefiting local distributors and assemblers like MLPT.

Local tech adoption in fintech and e-commerce underpins steady revenue growth for platform companies, though near-term volatility favors hardware plays over pure software.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's tech sector underperformed the US, but select movers like MLPT (+25%) and NBIS (+18.78%) signal strong local demand for niche hardware and AI infrastructure plays. Watch for follow-through on storage and semiconductor names (SNDK, WDC, MU) as global AI capex cycles lift Indonesia's component suppliers.

US-listed mining majors like FCX and NEM reflect a broader commodity super-cycle, with copper and gold demand underpinned by electrification and monetary policy easing.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's accelerating energy transition, driven by the 2060 net-zero target and new renewable energy law, creates durable demand for local solar, wind, and geothermal developers like BREN and VKTR.
The global push for energy security and decarbonization sustains growth in climate-tech subsectors, including hydrogen (PLUG) and grid-scale storage, benefiting from US and EU policy tailwinds.
Nickel-rich Indonesia is uniquely positioned to capture downstream value in battery supply chains, supporting long-term upside for domestic players in EV components and energy storage systems.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector shows steady gains, led by BREN (+8.29%) and VKTR (+5.81%), signaling continued domestic momentum. Capitalize on this by overweighting local players tied to the government's 2060 net-zero push and nickel-based energy storage supply chains, while selectively adding US-listed names like PLUG and CEG for hydrogen and nuclear diversification.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rising middle-class disposable income in Indonesia continues to drive premiumization in FMCG, benefiting companies with strong distribution in tier-2/3 cities.
Digital-native consumer brands are capturing share from legacy players, as e-commerce penetration deepens and Gen Z spending patterns shift toward convenience and aspirational products.
Government policies supporting local manufacturing and food self-sufficiency are creating structural tailwinds for domestic FMCG producers, reducing import dependency and margin volatility.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's consumer sector shows mild aggregate gains with a clear tilt toward small-cap recovery plays (ZATA +30%, AGAR +25%), signaling rotational risk-on appetite. Focus on domestic-demand-driven names like WMPP and BELL, as US weakness (-0.31%) creates relative safety in ID exposure. Maintain neutral positioning, but lean into sub-sectors with resilient local consumption trends.
